fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responding units can confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the driveway entry clearly on both sides to help responding units identify the turnoff, especially at night.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles and equipment along its full length to allow two-way movement for emergency vehicles.
• Confirm the driveway surface can support the weight of a fire apparatus or ambulance along its entire length.
• Identify and mark the locations of both detached structures with visible signage at the main driveway entrance so arriving units know what structures are on the property.
• Designate a staging area in the front driveway or open lawn area where emergency vehicles can park without blocking the access drive.
• Keep the access drive and open lawn area free of low-hanging branches that could obstruct tall emergency vehicles.
• Mark the water feature boundaries clearly so responders moving across the property at night or under stress can avoid it.
• Keep a gate, if present at the driveway entrance, unlocked or equipped with a rapid-access lock compatible with local fire department key systems.
• Post a simple site map at the driveway entrance showing the location of all structures, the water feature, and any secondary paths across the property.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches from trees that are close to the house to create separation between the tree canopy and the structure.
• Thin scattered trees near the house so they do not form a connected path from the surrounding vegetation to the structure.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or immediately next to the house.
• Cut grass near the house and outbuildings short, especially during dry periods.
• Thin the tree cluster nearest to any structure so individual trees are separated and do not touch each other.
• Keep the long driveway clear of overhanging branches so emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Remove dead branches, fallen limbs, and dry plant material from beneath trees near the house.
• Clear shrubs and tall grass from the edges of the driveway along its full length to maintain visibility and access.
• Remove any wood piles, stored materials, or other flammable items that are sitting directly against the house or outbuildings.
• Keep grass and low vegetation mowed short in open areas near the structures.
• Trim low-hanging branches from trees along the driveway to a height that allows a fire truck to pass beneath them.
